_meta.note: The backlog of shtetl, the ZFS-only successor to mishkan and parasa, built on zfs_rebase. One file for the whole project rather than one per sprint: milestones are planning.md section 12, plus "future" for work kept out of every milestone. Drive it with: python3 tools/tracker.py <cmd> (list, show, status, note). STATE 2026-10-12: M0 done; M1 and M2 built and passing on the box; M3 next.
_meta.coding_guidelines: the zfs rebase project's CLAUDE.md: ASCII only, cstyle, commits signed off as Eidel Solomon, a test matrix before tests

milestones.M2: discovery and multi-rooting, bootstrap, property table
milestones.M3: foundation build and update into zlake, patches and the pause; pkg-upgrade
milestones.M4: beam-down, new container, save with messages, the zlake mirror

_meta.worklogs: One markdown worklog per milestone or issue in docs/worklogs/, written when its code lands.

_schema.purpose: Field vocabulary for every issue object in this file. Use these exact terms; do not invent synonyms.

issue_fields.description: required, string. What to build and how to verify it.
issue_fields.requires: required, array of issue keys from THIS file. Empty array means no dependency.
issue_fields.milestone: required, the milestone this issue must be complete for, from _meta.milestones.
issue_fields.expected_changed_files: required, array of paths, relative to the repository root.
issue_fields.provides: required, string. What the rest of the work can rely on once this is tested.
issue_fields.estimated_size: required, one of: small | medium | large.
issue_fields.note: optional, string. Append with tracker.py note; never replace without cause.

status.code: implementation written and compiling, not yet exercised
status.testing: being exercised; tests being written or findings being fixed

patch-location-hosts.description: Settle how a patch source's location is told to be a host or a directory in zconfig (planning.md 7.1.1). Today (M1, src/core/syntax.c sh_syn_location; Q-X, accepted 2026-10-12 as good enough for now): a location with a scheme is a URL; with none, a location whose first component has a "." is a host, read as https, and anything else a directory in zconfig. So a zconfig directory whose first component has a dot cannot be named, a host is never checked, and a single-label host or an IP literal is not a host at all. To settle: which names count as hosts (the list of top-level domains changes, so a fixed list of gTLDs goes stale), single-label hosts, IP literals, a port. An idea of the author's to try first, being simple: try each dotted candidate, the whole name included, against DNS, and where none resolves, look for it locally in zconfig. That makes the reading depend on the network at the time of the build, which the build records (7.1.1, the record) and which is worth deciding knowingly. Verify: tests/MATRIX.md cells for every form, read both ways, and a build that names a source each way.
patch-location-hosts.provides: One rule for what a patch location is, holding for every name a person is likely to write.
patch-location-hosts.note: Raised by the author 2026-10-12 with the ruling on Q-X: "Good enough for now, put an issue on the backlog tracker ... in future work to nail down gtlds etc etc. In that future work issue we could also try a fairly simple solution of 'try every '.' including name against dns and if it fails, try to find it locally'."

kernconf-config-and-lines.description: Let one file give kernconf's config and its lines together. Today (src/core/schema.c, cascade.c mg_kernconf) kernconf is one key whose form decides its meaning: a quoted string is the config to start from, a heredoc the lines added to it. UCL takes a key once in a file, so a foundation that starts from a config of its own and adds lines to it gives one of the two in a file it imports. Forms to weigh: an object, kernconf { file = "MINE"; lines = <<EOD ... EOD }, beside the string and the heredoc; or nothing, the import being the answer. libucl takes no heredoc inside an array, so a list of the two is out. Verify: tests/MATRIX.md cells for the form chosen, alone and stacked with the default's config and lines, and configuration.md's kernconf section and examples run by make doc.
kernconf-config-and-lines.provides: A foundation's kernel config, its base and its lines, written in the one file of its recipe.
kernconf-config-and-lines.note: Raised 2026-10-12 with the kernconf rework (dcb2afc); the author: "Let's not concern ourselves with the UCL kernconf name + lines problem. let's just put this in future work."

m3-version.description: A foundation version's name (planning.md 6.1) and the ver check (7.1 step 1). From src_branch: releng/N.M is N.M-releng, stable/N is N-stable, main is <major>-current, the major asked of the checkout's sys/conf/newvers.sh (-V REVISION, a program, not a parse). With the build's date (UTC, ISO), the checkout's sha (12 characters, as uname shows it) and a counter for a second build the same day from the same sha (.2, .3, from the names F's snapshots have): @15.1-releng-2026-10-08-0f691888dc56. The ver check: before the checkout, the version src_branch names (N.M, or every N.x for stable/N) must meet every ver of the recipe; after it, newvers.sh's REVISION must satisfy them all. Portable. Verify: tests/MATRIX.md family V before tests/check_version.c.
m3-version.provides: The name and the version check every build and update use.

m3-zfs.description: The ZFS calls a build needs, in src/core/zfs.h with the fake (tests/zfake.c) and libzfs (src/fbsd/zfs.c): a recursive snapshot with user properties, atomic (lzc_snapshot); a dataset's snapshots with createtxg, guid and shtetl:kind; rollback to a snapshot; a snapshot destroyed; a property set and inherited; a filesystem and its children mounted and unmounted. Verify: MATRIX cells for the fake's behavior (it is what the build's tests stand on), and tools/xcheck-freebsd.sh for the libzfs side; the box for the libzfs side's behavior.
m3-zfs.provides: Everything the build asks of ZFS, faked faithfully enough to test the build on the mac.
m3-zfs.note: Box run 3 (dc2be99) green: 95 ok, Z11 - Z13 on libzfs.

m3-build.description: shtetl build F for a new foundation (planning.md 7.1, without patches): the recipe resolved and checked; the plan shown and confirmed as bootstrap's is (-y); one build at a time (shtetl:build on the src root); the config root snapshotted and the snapshot recorded (4.4, shtetl:config); zlake/foundations/F pre-split before anything is installed; the checkout of src_branch in zbuild; the kernel config and src.conf shtetl writes (kernconf, buildopts); make buildworld buildkernel with MAKEOBJDIRPREFIX on foundation-builds/F; installworld, installkernel and distribution with INSTALL_CMD="install -C"; pkg and commands in a chroot of F; snapshot -r with the version name and shtetl:kind, shtetl:commit, shtetl:config, shtetl:patches; every mount undone on every way out. Programs from a table the tests point at fakes. Verify: MATRIX family F (the build) before its tests, over the fake ZFS and fake make, git and pkg; the box for a real build.
m3-build.provides: A foundation built from its recipe into zlake, one version snapshot.
m3-build.note: Box build 2 (dc2be99) green: 26 ok; a real releng/15.1 build into box@15.1-releng-2026-10-13-e38a7085f3a8.

m3-kernel-install.description: The kernel installed through a scratch DESTDIR (planning.md 7.2 as built): installkernel into F removes its /boot/kernel first (sys/conf/kern.post.mk keeps a .old only over the running kernel's directory), so every update wrote every kernel file anew. installkernel into the obj cache's kernel-install, then synced into F as install -C would: a file alike left as it is, a changed or new one copied in, boot/kernel and usr/lib/debug/boot/kernel mirrored. Verify: MATRIX F34 on the mac; the box, an unchanged module keeping its object across F27's update.

m4-zfs.description: The ZFS calls of M4 (src/core/zfs.h), over libzfs_core, no zfs(8): a clone of a snapshot with properties from its birth (lzc_clone); a snapshot sent and received, whole, incremental, or as a clone stream received as a clone of another (lzc_send into lzc_receive through a pipe, no property travelling); the user properties set on a snapshot itself, walked (to copy shtetl:* after a receive, 6.2); a clone's origin read. Verify: MATRIX family Z (Z14 -) over the fake; the box (tests/box/zcheck.c, across two pools).
m4-zfs.provides: Clones and sends for beam-down, create and save.

m4-beam.description: A foundation's version brought to zrun (planning.md 7.3): each dataset of F sent from zlake, whole the first time, incremental from the newest version zrun has after; received under the run root's foundations/F, readonly=on, canmount=noauto, a placeholder canmount=off, the mountpoint inherited; no -p, the version's shtetl:* copied onto each received snapshot after (6.2), a received snapshot with no shtetl:kind copied again. The command (PROPOSAL): shtetl beam F [--version V]; create does it when the version is not there. Verify: MATRIX family M; the box.
m4-beam.provides: Foundation versions on zrun to clone containers from.

m4-save.description: shtetl save X [-m msg] (planning.md 7.5, 6.2): zfs snapshot -r of the container with shtetl:kind=save, shtetl:commit (-m, or written in an editor) and shtetl:config; the zlake mirror (7.10): each dataset into the lake root's containers/X, a foundation-inherited dataset's first save a clone stream received as a clone of zlake's F/d@vN, a container-only dataset's first a full stream, later saves incremental from the previous; shtetl:* copied after each receive. Retention's prune is M7. Verify: MATRIX family S; the box.
m4-save.provides: Saves with messages on zrun, mirrored in zlake as deltas.

m4-create.description: shtetl create X --on F [--version V] (planning.md 7.4): the checks (X's ver allows the version, its datasets do not collide with F's); the version beamed if not on zrun; a clone per dataset of F@v parent first, a placeholder -o canmount=off, the recipe's properties set locally; X's own datasets; the jail block written and the jail started; pkg -j X install and the commands, a piece the foundation ran as of its shtetl:config left out; the first save. The jail's particulars (where its block lives, what it holds, how commands run in it, requires) are PROPOSALs. Verify: MATRIX family X; the box.
m4-create.provides: Containers on zrun, cloned from a foundation version, saved.

m5-cutover.description: shtetl cutover X and shtetl abandon X (planning.md 7.9, 7.10): cutover asks about writes to X since its from-save (written@), promotes X-staging's own clones, destroys the old X on zrun, renames X-staging to X, its jail block with it, starts and saves X; in zlake the same promotes, the old X moved to archive/containers/X-<ISO-date>, the staging mirror renamed. abandon stops and destroys X-staging, on zrun and in zlake, and starts X. Verify: MATRIX family K; the box.

Ruled 2026-10-15 (planning.md 14, 12.1). Verify: create and update read the foundation's recipe from the file; families F, P, X, U.
m6-recipe-file.provides: A snapshot that says, in itself, what recipe made it.
